titles.tagline: Every Island Has a Warrior. Every Rhythm Has a Weapon.

universe.summary: OPAIJA is a Caribbean Afrocentric martial anime rooted in Trinidad and Tobago stick-fighting traditions, Carnival energy, ancestral rhythm, folklore, drums, lavway chants, and sacred bois.
universe.opaija_seeds: Fragmented ancestral staffs hidden during the transatlantic slave trade and scattered across Caribbean islands. Each island's culture, rhythm, and environment transformed the fragments into unique power systems.

core_lore.hidden_method: The sacred bois were NOT smuggled whole. They were broken into: drum pegs, walking cane fragments, carved beads, ship repair wood, pestle handles, prayer objects, hair ornaments, children's toys, pieces of firewood, carved marks under skin scars, and songs (lavway).
core_lore.key_truth: The enemy thought they had taken every weapon. But they did not know the weapon had been hidden inside rhythm.
core_lore.the_lavway_secret: The real secret was not only the wood. It was the lavway — the call-and-response chant that told future generations how to awaken the sticks.
core_lore.historical_anchor: Approximately 44,000 enslaved Africans were brought to Trinidad and Tobago through the transatlantic slave trade. The people of African descent arrived enslaved, liberated, or free during the 17th to 19th centuries.
core_lore.stick_fighting_roots: Kalenda/Calinda — Caribbean martial dance from Trinidad and Tobago, weapon-based, using sticks (bois), accompanied by vocals and drums, based on traditional African combat dances. Canboulay and stick fights dominated Carnival in the second half of the 19th century.

power_system.name: The Five-Part Opaija System
power_system.core_rule: A stick has memory. A fighter has spirit. A drum has rhythm. A lavway has command. The gayelle binds them together.

five_parts.bois_memory: The stick stores ancestral combat knowledge. Older sticks = deeper memory. A stick chooses its fighter.
five_parts.inner_pulse: The fighter's own spiritual rhythm — their unique beat. Must be discovered, not taught.
five_parts.lavway_command: Call-and-response chants that activate specific abilities. Must be sung correctly — intent matters.
five_parts.drum_sync: Alignment with a drummer partner amplifies all powers. Jabs is Kai's drum sync partner.
five_parts.gayelle_vow: A sacred oath taken in the gayelle circle. Binds fighter to their bois permanently. Cannot be undone.

power_system.awakening_rule: A person CANNOT just pick up a sacred stick and become powerful. The stick only awakens when all five conditions align.

villain_opposite.name: Silence Pulse
villain_opposite.description: Marius Vale's system. Suppresses rhythm, erases memory, disconnects fighters from their bois. The antithesis of everything OPAIJA stands for.
villain_opposite.visual: Silence cracks instead of rhythm glyphs. Black void spreads where Silence Pulse activates.

combat_visual_language: Drumbeat rings — circular pulses visible on impact
Rhythm glyphs — circular symbols that appear when powers activate
Bois energy carvings — glowing lines along the staff when memory activates
Sound-wave effects tied to beat timing
Silence cracks — villain-only, black fractures in the visual field
Motion MUST be tied to beat timing — every strike lands on a beat

language_rules.patois_rule: Use patois in CHARACTER dialogue and CAPTION only. The Web-Teller narrator uses standard English with Caribbean rhythm. Never use patois in ways that mock or otherness — it is a mark of authenticity and cultural pride.
language_rules.patois_max_per_episode: 2-3 lines, character dialogue/captions only, never in narration

villain_reveal_schedule.episodes_1_6: Marius Vale is unseen. Only felt through agents and Silence Pulse effects.
villain_reveal_schedule.episode_7: First silhouette reveal — back only, no face
villain_reveal_schedule.episode_12: Marius Vale speaks directly to Kai

selah_reveal: Selah Vale appears episode 8. Her connection to Marius is revealed episode 9.
doubles_rule: Kai MUST have a doubles moment in every episode. This is non-negotiable. It may be brief — a grab, a bite, a vendor interaction — but it must be present.

doubles_lore.what_is_doubles: Trinidad's most beloved street food. Two fried bara (soft fried flatbread) filled with curried chickpeas (channa). Topped with coconut chutney, pepper sauce, and tamarind. Eaten wrapped in paper, standing up, at a roadside stall.
doubles_lore.kai_rule: Kai eats doubles before every significant moment. It is his ritual. Full belly. Steady spirit. When stressed, he finds a vendor. When nervous before a fight, he finds a vendor. Mother Lall is his preferred source.
doubles_lore.comedy_note: The doubles quest is a recurring comedic beat. Kai will delay important things to get doubles. His team is exasperated. He is unapologetic.
doubles_lore.merch_opportunity: Doubles gag merch — sticker packs, 'Full Belly. Steady Spirit.' tees, Kai doubles charm

episode_beat_map.5_20_sec: CONFLICT — establish the problem or tension
episode_beat_map.20_45_sec: REVEAL — something changes or is discovered
episode_beat_map.final_seconds: CLIFFHANGER — must end with a question or danger

narration_style: One narrator (The Web-Teller). Minimal dialogue. Character acting through expression and body language. Patois used sparingly — max 2–3 lines per episode for authenticity without alienating international viewers.

kai_baptiste.role: Main hero / First Opaija Seed wielder
kai_baptiste.weapon: The Listening Bois — carved by Elders, hears rhythm, channels beat, protects its people

nia_toussaint.signature_line: Doh sing it unless yuh mean it.
nia_toussaint.quirk: Always hums under her breath when nervous

malik_st_hill.weapon: Rootbreaker Bois — straight, polished, hardened tip
malik_st_hill.quirk: Always reties his sash before a serious fight

asha_singh_baptiste.signature_line: History does leave marks. Allyuh just not looking.
asha_singh_baptiste.quirk: Keeps notes and sketches in the margins of any scrap paper

jabari_henry.power: Drum Sync — amplifies all team members' powers when drumming
jabari_henry.weapon: Traditional wooden African Kalinda drums — NOT modern kit. L-shaped drum sticks (curved, traditional style).
jabari_henry.quirk: Films everything on his phone. Documents the team for his channel. Running commentary on everything.

tariq_davidson.weapon: Tidewatch Bois — driftwood core, shell inlay, sea glass. Channels Tide Pulse and Silent Beat.
tariq_davidson.signature_line: That doh mean allyuh own the whole sea.
tariq_davidson.quirk: Collects shells and small driftwood carvings from every beach he visits

mother_lall.role: Doubles Vendor / Secret Guardian Messenger / Hidden Lore Keeper

papa_etienne_roach.weapon: Cane — not a bois. He gave up his bois. That is a story for season 2.
papa_etienne_roach.signature_line: The stick is not a gift. It is a debt.

marius_vale.role: Main Villain / False One Drum / Silence Strategist
marius_vale.power: Silence Pulse — suppresses all rhythm-based powers
marius_vale.weapon: The One Drum — a corrupted Opaija Seed that broadcasts Silence Pulse
marius_vale.signature_line: One drum. One command. One Caribbean.

visual_style.description: 2D anime characters on 3D cinematic camera movements. Hand-drawn impact effects. Stylized rhythm glyphs. Painterly Caribbean environments.

face_rules.nose: Broad African-Caribbean nose structure — not narrow anime noses
face_rules.lips: Full lips — not thin anime defaults
face_rules.skin: Rich melanin tones — warm browns, deep ebonies, golden undertones
face_rules.eyes: Expressive anime eyes but grounded in Caribbean features
DO_NOT: Use pale skin for Caribbean characters
Make characters look like constant cosplay

visual_style.hair_rules: All characters must have textured, Afro-Caribbean or Caribbean-influenced hairstyles. Locs, braids, twists, high-tops, coils. Each character's hair is their signature.

style_locks: Jabari's drums are AFRICAN STYLE WOODEN, L-SHAPED sticks — ALWAYS
power_system_limits: No fighter can use Opaija power without their specific bois — the power does not transfer between sticks unless lore specifically allows
Silence Pulse cannot be permanently destroyed in Season 1
Lavway Command requires correct singing — humming or speaking it does not activate it
Drum Sync requires the drummer to be physically present or within earshot
Gayelle Vow cannot be undone once taken
